# SQLite Block Demo

This runbook demonstrates the `<SQLite>` block. Each block runs a SQL query
against a local SQLite database file and shows the result as a table.

## Create a table

<SQLite
  id="create-users"
  db="./demo.db"
  query="CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT)"
  title="Create the users table"
  description="Creates the `users` table if it doesn't exist yet."
/>

## Insert rows

<SQLite
  id="insert-alice"
  db="./demo.db"
  query="INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES (?, ?)"
  params={["Alice", "alice@example.com"]}
  title="Insert Alice"
/>

<SQLite
  id="insert-bob"
  db="./demo.db"
  query="INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES (?, ?)"
  params={["Bob", null]}
  title="Insert Bob (no email)"
/>

## Query the data

<SQLite
  id="list-users"
  db="./demo.db"
  query="SELECT id, name, email FROM users ORDER BY id"
  output="users"
  title="List all users"
  description="Selects every row from the users table. The result is exported as the `users` output."
  successMessage="Users loaded!"
/>

<SQLite
  id="count-users"
  db="./demo.db"
  query="SELECT COUNT(*) AS total FROM users"
  title="Count users"
/>

## Error case

<SQLite
  id="bad-query"
  db="./demo.db"
  query="SELECT * FROM nonexistent_table"
  title="This query will fail"
  description="Demonstrates the error state of the block."
  failMessage="Query failed as expected"
/>

## Test on Navidrome

<SQLite
  id="test-nv"
  db="./navidrome.db"
  query="SELECT album, album_artist
    FROM playlist_tracks
      INNER JOIN media_file mf ON media_file_id = mf.id
    WHERE playlist_id = (
      SELECT id FROM playlist WHERE name = 'Validé'
    ) AND path LIKE 'validated%'
    GROUP BY album, album_artist;"
  title="Tests"
/>

## Run a SQL file

<SQLite
  id="seed-from-file"
  db="./demo.db"
  path="./scripts/seed.sql"
  title="Seed from a .sql file"
  description="Executes every statement in scripts/seed.sql (multi-statement)."
/>
